numerical_failure.observed_behavior: scipy.linalg.pinvh computes results that do not satisfy the Moore-Penrose conditions; for the Hermitian matrix [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]] the check np.allclose(y1 @ x @ y1, y1) is False, and the results substantially differ from scipy.linalg.pinv. SYEVR (the 'evr' eigh driver) may give a zero eigenvalue greater than epsilon, with the reported eigenvalues being about -3.37e-17 or 3.93e-17 instead of 0 for that matrix.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: pinvh should return a pseudoinverse satisfying the Moore-Penrose conditions, matching scipy.linalg.pinv for the same matrix; the analytically computed eigenvalues of the example matrix are 3, 1, and 0.
trigger_conditions: Hermitian input matrix whose near-zero eigenvalue is computed by the SYEVR ('evr') eigh driver, e.g. x = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]]
pinvh uses default eigh driver (evr) before the fix; the default condition number/rcond cutoff does not discard the spurious tiny eigenvalue
Setting a larger cutoff such as pinvh(a, rcond=1e-14) returns sensible results according to the issue discussion

input_output_examples.buggy_output: np.allclose(np.matmul(np.matmul(y1, x), y1), y1) returns False
input_output_examples.expected_output: np.allclose(np.matmul(np.matmul(y1, x), y1), y1) returns True (y1 should match pinv(x))

input_output_examples.input: sp.linalg.eigh(a, driver='evr') on the same matrix
